Title: Geely BHE / i-HEV reaches 48.41% peak thermal efficiency
Context: GE HEV / PHEV engine Efficiency (#23, #25) · DieselNet, Apr 2026
Body: Above the maximum of the adopted range. If confirmed on a homologated cycle, it favours HEV/PHEV and SPHEV over BEV on a cradle-to-grave basis.

Title: Chery: 48% prototype (26:1, Miller cycle) and 44.5% in the production 1.5 TDGI
Context: GE HEV engine Efficiency (#23) and GE Compact (#18) · Auto Motor und Sport, Nov 2025
Body: The production figure (44.5%) already exceeds the adopted maximum, suggesting the PET range for HEVs may be conservative.

Title: Nissan e-POWER third generation: 1.5 turbo generator engine at ~42%
Context: Range Extender Combustion Engine Efficiency (#32) · InsideEVs Brasil
Body: Within the range, above the most frequent value. Reinforces SPHEV/SHEV as a transition option.

Title: Aramco Dedicated Hybrid Engine (DHE): 41% in a hybrid-dedicated engine
Context: Range Extender Combustion Engine Efficiency (#32) · Aramco Americas, 2026
Body: Within the range. Relevant for emerging markets with biofuels — the Brazilian case.

Title: CATL condensed-matter cell at 350 Wh/kg — a 125 kWh pack weighing ~625 kg (≈5.0 kg/kWh)
Context: Energy Battery Density reciprocal (#48) · Zecar, CATL Tech Day 2026
Reported: ≈2.86 kg/kWh at cell level · ≈5.0 kg/kWh at pack level
Body: The announced pack-level figure already approaches the adopted best case. It lowers BEV mass, pulling down both manufacturing and energy use — favours BEV.

Title: Battery manufacturing: 50–100 kg CO2e/kWh typical, 10–25 with renewable electricity
Context: Energy Battery Carbon Intensity reciprocal (#62) · electrive, Aug 2025
Body: The adopted minimum (44.1) sits far above what cells produced on a clean grid already achieve. Given the Brazilian low-carbon electricity mix, this is the parameter with the greatest potential to shift the result in favour of BEVs.

Title: Stanford / Nature Energy: degradation up to 38% slower in real-world use; service life up to ~300,000 km
Context: Battery Lifespan (#55) and Usable Battery Capacity factor (#34) · Gadget Review (on the Stanford / Nature Energy study)
Adopted: battery lifespan MF 200 · max 300 thousand km
Body: Pushes battery lifespan towards the top of the range, diluting manufacturing emissions per km — favours BEV and PHEV.

Title: Geotab (22,700 vehicles): average degradation of 2.3%/year, ~82% SoH after 8 years
Context: BEV lifetime-average Usable Battery Capacity factor (#34) · New Atlas / Geotab 2025
Body: Suggests 0.75 is conservative for recent fleets. The i3ET has no explicit annual-degradation parameter — it is embedded in this factor.
